source_refs.note: Topic 25.3 with Quick Check 25.3, answered (PDF 139-141); the schemes are redrawn. The note on sodium phenoxide (Kolbe-Schmitt) and the 2-nitrophenol by-product go beyond the book. Answers need review.

blocks.text: One of the most important applications of retrosynthesis is in making pharmaceutical products. Many valuable medicines have complex structures, but if they are disconnected properly and efficiently, they can be traced back to very simple, common starting materials.

blocks.alt: Phenol (HO on a benzene ring) followed by four short arrows labelled 'A series of steps' leading to paracetamol, HO on a benzene ring with N(H)-C(=O)-CH3 at the opposite position.
blocks.caption: Direct synthesis of paracetamol (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 139).

items: Disconnect the amide C-N bond: the synthons are HO-C6H4-NH- and CH3CO+.
Synthetic equivalents: 4-aminophenol and ethanoyl (acyl) chloride; these are known to react by nucleophilic addition-elimination.
FGI: 4-aminophenol comes from 4-nitrophenol, which is easy to prepare and can be reduced.
Disconnect the C-N bond of 4-nitrophenol: the synthons are the 4-hydroxyphenyl anion and NO2+.
Synthetic equivalents: phenol and nitric acid.

blocks.alt: Five steps. I: paracetamol with a wavy slash on the amide C-N bond, Disconnection, gives HO-C6H4-N(-)H, synthon (A), plus +C(=O)CH3, synthon (B). II: synthon (A) equals 4-aminophenol (SE); synthon (B) equals acyl chloride (SE). III: 4-aminophenol, FGI open arrow, 4-nitrophenol. IV: 4-nitrophenol slashed at the C-NO2 bond gives HO-C6H4 with a negative charge, synthon (A), plus NO2+, synthon (B). V: these equal phenol (SE) and nitric acid HO-NO2 (SE).
blocks.caption: Retrosynthesis of paracetamol, Steps I-V (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 139-140).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Step III of the printed scheme uses a forward reaction arrow from 4-aminophenol to 4-nitrophenol; a functional group interconversion in retrosynthesis takes the open retrosynthetic arrow, as drawn above.
Synthesis: phenol is nitrated to 4-nitrophenol (HNO3), the nitro group is reduced with Sn and HCl to give 4-aminophenol, and this reacts with ethanoyl chloride to give paracetamol, HO-C6H4-NHCOCH3.

blocks.alt: Phenol, labelled phenol (SM), with HNO3 over and H2SO4 under the arrow gives 4-nitrophenol; Sn + HCl gives 4-aminophenol; a downward arrow labelled CH3COCl gives paracetamol, labelled Paracetamol (TM).
blocks.caption: Synthesis of paracetamol (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 140).

blocks.alt: Phenol followed by four short arrows labelled 'A series of steps' leading to aspirin: a benzene ring with COOH and, on the neighbouring carbon, O-C(=O)-CH3.
blocks.caption: Direct synthesis of aspirin (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 140).

items: Disconnect the ester C-O bond: the synthons are the 2-carboxyphenoxide ion and CH3CO+.
Synthetic equivalents: salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) and ethanoic (acetic) anhydride.
Disconnect the C-C bond of the carboxyl group in salicylic acid: the synthons are the 2-hydroxyphenyl anion and +COOH.
Synthetic equivalents: phenol and carbon dioxide.

blocks.alt: Four steps. I: aspirin (TM) with a wavy slash on the ester O-C bond, Disconnection, gives the 2-carboxyphenoxide ion, synthon (A), plus +C(=O)CH3, synthon (B). II: synthon (A) equals salicylic acid (SE); synthon (B) equals acetic anhydride (SE). III: salicylic acid slashed at the ring-COOH bond gives a ring carbanion next to OH, (A) synthon, plus +C(=O)OH, (B) synthon. IV: these equal phenol (SE) and carbon dioxide O=C=O (SE).
blocks.caption: Retrosynthesis of aspirin, Steps I-IV (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 141).

blocks.text: Synthesis: phenol reacts with carbon dioxide at high pressure, and acidification with H2SO4 gives salicylic acid; heating salicylic acid with ethanoic anhydride and an H3PO4 catalyst gives aspirin.

blocks.alt: Phenol (SM) with (i) CO2, High T & P over and (ii) H2SO4 under the arrow gives salicylic acid; acetic anhydride drawn over and H3PO4, Heat under the next arrow gives Aspirin (TM).
blocks.caption: Synthesis of aspirin (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 141).

items: Aspirin and paracetamol are both made from phenol. What is the overall functional group difference between them?
Which FGI is involved in their syntheses?
Which synthon is common to both preparations? Give its structure and its usual synthetic equivalent.
